title: Symphony No. 2 in C minor, “Resurrection”
hook: It opens at a funeral and ends with a choir singing of rising again.

painting.title: The Resurrection (Isenheim Altarpiece)
painting.pairingNote: Christ rises in a blaze of light while the guards tumble, the moment the finale sings about. The 1963 American LP of this very recording carried a detail of the same altarpiece.

facts: Written between 1888 and 1894. The first movement began as a separate funeral piece, *Totenfeier* (Funeral Rites). Mahler conducted the first complete performance in Berlin on 13 December 1895.

For years he could not find an ending. At the conductor Hans von Bülow’s funeral in 1894 he heard a sung setting of Klopstock’s hymn “Die Auferstehung” (The Resurrection). It struck him “like lightning”. He kept the first verses and wrote the rest of the text himself.
The forces are huge: soprano and alto soloists, a choir, an organ, church bells, and horns, trumpets and drums placed [[offstage|offstage]], out of sight.
Mahler asked for a pause of five minutes after the first movement. Most performances take a shorter break.
bigPicture.inOneLine: a funeral (I), a memory of happy days (II), life as an empty whirl (III), a simple prayer (IV), the end of the world and a resurrection (V).

movements.heading: Allegro maestoso
movements.title: Allegro maestoso
movements.summary: A funeral, and a question: is there anything after death? Violent outbursts alternate with a tender melody that seems to come from another, happier world.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1
mainIdeas.description: a furious growl in the cellos and basses under trembling violins.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2
mainIdeas.description: a soft, rising melody in the violins, in a bright and distant key.

stops.hear: Violins and violas shiver; cellos and basses snarl upwards, again and again
stops.happening: The opening. Mahler marks it “with complete gravity and solemnity”

stops.hear: Heavy, marching chords in the full orchestra, then wailing woodwinds
stops.happening: The funeral march

stops.hear: The storm clears. Violins sing a gentle, rising melody
stops.happening: Theme 2, in E major, far from the home key

stops.hear: The snarling basses return
stops.happening: The themes are presented again, changed

stops.hear: Quiet: harp, cor anglais and violins drift in a pastoral dream
stops.happening: The start of the [[development|development]]

stops.hear: Low woodwinds and brass intone a slow, solemn tune
stops.happening: The [[dies-irae|Dies irae]], the chant for the dead, which will return in the finale

stops.hear: The music piles up to a shattering climax and falls down a chromatic scale
stops.happening: The crisis of the movement

stops.hear: The opening shiver and snarl, at full force
stops.happening: The [[recapitulation|recapitulation]]

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: A plunging scale in the full orchestra, then a few hard chords
stops.happening: The funeral ends in C minor, without answers

notice: Mahler wanted silence after this movement. If you can, pause here before going on.

movements.heading: Andante moderato
movements.title: Andante moderato
movements.summary: A slow, graceful country dance, “never hurried”, like a snapshot of happier days. Two darker episodes interrupt it.

stops.hear: Strings in a gentle, swaying tune in three
stops.happening: A [[landler|Ländler]], a slow Austrian country dance

stops.hear: Running triplets in the strings, more restless
stops.happening: The first episode

stops.hear: The dance returns; cellos add a warm countermelody underneath
stops.happening: The Ländler, richer

stops.hear: The running figures return, louder, with brass
stops.happening: The second episode, now stormy

stops.hear: The dance tune again, but now the strings pluck it
stops.happening: The tune played [[pizzicato|pizzicato]], light as a memory

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: Harp and soft strings fade out
stops.happening: The memory closes

movements.heading: In ruhig fließender Bewegung
movements.title: In ruhig fließender Bewegung (Scherzo)
movements.summary: A [[scherzo|scherzo]] that never stops flowing. It is based on Mahler’s song about Saint Anthony preaching to the fishes, who listen, nod, and swim off unchanged. Under the humour lies a view of life as pointless motion.

stops.hear: Two hard timpani strokes, then softer ones; violins start an endless winding line
stops.happening: The scherzo begins

stops.hear: A shrill clarinet plays a sly, slightly tipsy tune
stops.happening: The humour turns sour

stops.hear: Trumpets and strings in a brighter, more open tune
stops.happening: The [[trio|trio]]

stops.hear: The winding violins return
stops.happening: The scherzo again

stops.hear: The flow breaks off in a huge, dissonant scream from the full orchestra
stops.happening: Mahler called this a “cry of despair”. It will open the finale

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: The winding line runs on, thinner, and stops
stops.happening: Motion without meaning

movements.heading: Urlicht
movements.title: Urlicht (Primal Light)
movements.summary: After the scream, a prayer. An alto sings a simple song from *Des Knaben Wunderhorn* (The Boy’s Magic Horn), the German folk-poetry collection Mahler loved: a soul longing for God and for release from pain.

stops.hear: The alto alone sings “O Röschen rot!” (O little red rose)
stops.happening: The voice enters with no introduction

stops.hear: Soft brass, low and hushed, like a distant hymn
stops.happening: A [[chorale|chorale]] in trumpets, horns and bassoons

stops.hear: The pace quickens; a solo violin glitters
stops.happening: In the poem an angel tries to turn the singer away. The singer refuses

stops.hear: The voice rises, slow and certain
stops.happening: The soul will find its way back to God

stops.label: Last seconds
stops.hear: A long, quiet chord
stops.happening: The finale bursts in almost at once

movements.heading: Im Tempo des Scherzos
movements.title: Im Tempo des Scherzos
movements.summary: Half an hour of music in two parts. First the orchestra alone: the end of the world, the dead marching out of their graves, voices calling from far away. Then, out of total silence, a choir sings of resurrection.

stops.hear: The scream from the third movement crashes in at full force
stops.happening: The finale begins

stops.hear: Distant horns call from out of sight over hushed strings
stops.happening: The first [[offstage|offstage]] call, a voice from far away

stops.hear: Soft woodwinds, then a quiet, noble tune in the trombones
stops.happening: The [[dies-irae|Dies irae]], then the resurrection theme the choir will sing

stops.hear: Two long drum rolls swell from nothing to a roar
stops.happening: The dead rise. A frantic march begins

stops.hear: A pleading melody in the orchestra while a band offstage blares and thunders
stops.happening: The march collapses into chaos

stops.hear: Horns and trumpets call from far away; a flute imitates a bird above the silence
stops.happening: Mahler’s “great summons”, the last call before judgement

stops.hear: The choir enters almost inaudibly, the orchestra nearly silent: “Aufersteh’n” (Rise again)
stops.happening: Klopstock’s hymn. The soprano soars out of the choir

stops.hear: The alto sings an urgent plea
stops.happening: Mahler’s own words begin: “O believe, my heart”

stops.hear: Soprano and alto in duet, then the choir rises on “wings”
stops.happening: The music climbs towards E-flat major

stops.hear: Full choir, organ and orchestra at maximum power, then pealing bells
stops.happening: The resurrection. The bells ring out to the end

notice: Listen for the space: some of the brass is meant to come from outside the hall. In a good recording you can hear the distance.
The choir’s first entry is marked to be sung as quietly as possible. Turn the volume up a little before ≈ 21:30, not after.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Klemperer knew the symphony from the inside. In 1905, aged 20, he was put in charge of the offstage band at a Berlin performance, met Mahler there, and later got his first conducting post on Mahler’s recommendation.

threads.title: From funeral to resurrection
threads.body: The symphony starts in C minor, at a graveside, and ends in E-flat major, in light.

threads.title: The chant for the dead
threads.body: The [[dies-irae|Dies irae]] appears in the first movement and again in the finale, where the resurrection theme finally answers it.

threads.title: Near and far
threads.body: Calls from offstage horns, trumpets and drums give the symphony a sense of distance that no other work of its time had.
